## Rule

**Fill 3×3 all-background holes with blue.** Generator `task_6cf79266` (size=20): a dense
single-color 20×20 grid with 1–3 black (color-0) 3×3 cutouts. A 3×3 block that is entirely
black gets repainted blue (color 1). Decoded from the SHIPPED PARENT initializers (2026-05-31),
which solves it 266/266 — so this is a normally-scored task (Path-A gain = raw `log_e(cost ratio)` × 1.0×, not an unlock).

## Algorithm sketch

```python
black  = input[:, 0]                       # color-0 channel (W0=[1,0,..,0] picks it)
sum3   = conv3x3_sum(black)                # count of black in the 3x3 block anchored top-left at (r,c)
anchor = (sum3 == 9)                        # block all-black  (Greater(sum3, 8.5))
# top-left dedupe of an adjacent-anchor cluster (matches the generator's sequential scan):
primary = anchor & ~anchor[r-1,c] & ~anchor[r,c-1] & ~anchor[r-1,c-1]
fill    = dilate3x3(primary) > 0            # union of each primary's 3x3 block
output  = where(fill, blue, input)          # fill cells were black -> become blue
```
Parent realizes the dedupe with 2 shift-Convs (`WSD1/WSR1=[1,0,0]`) + Pad/Slice (diag) + 3×`Sub(1,·)`
+ `Where` + 2×`Mul`, and the paint with `delta=Where(gt2,[-1,+1,0..],0)` then `Add(input_cropped,delta)` then `Pad`.

## Cost analysis

**LIVE FLOOR = 3,496 — Sho `task162_scaled_cast` (opset 18), proven minimal by worker3 2026-07-11.**
`score_network_v2` = (macs 0, memory 3320, params 176). Graph: `Conv → Cast(int8) → MaxPool → Cast(bool) → Pad → Where`. The scaled 4×4 conv (weight ×1/9.1, pads `[1,1,-10,-10]`) fuses anchor+dedupe; the `Cast(F32→int8)` truncation IS the threshold. Every tensor is a forced component:

| tensor | dtype | bytes | why locked |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `seed_score` [1,1,18,18] | F32 | 1296 | 4×4 Conv **directly on the F32 input** (no ch0 slice). Conv F32→F32; 18×18 = the exact 3×3-anchor grid in 20×20. No ONNX op reduces F32→int8 in one step, so the first materialized plane is F32. |
| `seed_i8` [1,1,18,18] | INT8 | 324 | Cast target = the anchor/dedupe threshold; needed so dilation runs in int8 (F32 MaxPool = 1600 — see P2). |
| `cover_i8` [1,1,20,20] | INT8 | 400 | MaxPool 3×3 dilation. ORT rule `pad<kernel` caps output at 20×20 — cannot reach 30×30 (see P1). |
| `cover` [1,1,20,20] | BOOL | 400 | Cast(int8→bool); Where needs BOOL. Cheapest to cast at 20×20 before padding. |
| `mark` [1,1,30,30] | BOOL | 900 | Pad to the 30×30 canvas; Where output is 30×30 so the condition must be 30×30. Data-dependent 2-D union, NOT separable/free-output (worker1: techniques #67/#81/#89 don't dissolve it). |

memory 3320 + params 176 (conv `[1,10,4,4]`=160 avoids a 1600-B ch0 slice; oh1 10 + pad 4 + axes 2) = **3,496**.

**Why sub-3496 is impossible (WALL).** The rule forces the topology `linear-conv → nonlinear threshold → nonlinear dilate → canvas mask → Where` — a single conv/Einsum output for ch0 is LP-infeasible (`hard_records/grouped_finalconv_linear.md`), so the threshold+dilate stages cannot be folded into the conv. Each intermediate above is at its minimal legal size:
- **Head F32 (1296) is forced.** Any spatial reduction (Conv/Pool/MatMul) on the F32 input yields F32; producing int8 seeds needs a post-reduction Cast, so the 1296 F32 plane must exist first. Slicing/quantizing ch0 first costs ≥1600 (worse). F16 conv needs F16 input (Cast input = 18000).
- **Tail is forced.** P1 proves you cannot merge dilation+canvas (`MaxPool pad<kernel` is a hard ORT error). P2 proves the early int8 cast is load-bearing (F32 pool = +878). Padding int8 to 30×30 before the bool cast is worse (900+900 vs 400+900).
- **Params forced at 176.** 10-channel conv avoids the slice; oh1 must be the [1,10,1,1] blue one-hot; axes-form Pad (4+2) beats full pads[8].

worker3 built both probes (`prototypes/build_task162_bo_ng_cld_worker3_floor.py`): P2 f32-pool = 4374, P1 merge30 = ORT-illegal. Both LOSE. Full record: `hard_records/scaled_cast_floor_3496.md`.

## Don't-do log

- **Don't blanket-f16 (onnxconverter_common / `pass_fp16_selective`).** The 2026-05-20 PR_HUGE worker
  tried it → NO WIN (Cast-wrapper overhead > savings / broke output type / failed ORT load). Surgical
  per-tensor placement is required. Naive "Cast after Slice" on `input_cropped` is a NET LOSS: it leaves
  the F32 [1,10,20,20] (16k) AND adds an F16 copy (8k) = 24k > 16k.
- **Don't drop the `primary` dedupe** to "just dilate all anchors" (the sub-floor temptation). MEASURED
  2026-05-31 via `build_task162_v3_unsafe.py` (cost 6,548, would-be +2.39 LB): `fill = dilate(anchor)` is a
  morphological OPENING and **FAILS 1/266 visible** (the dedupe is load-bearing even within the official
  pairs) and **diverges 77.7%** on adjacent-hole synth. Fresh ARC-GEN `generate()` shows 0/2000 because the
  generator self-filters via its `legal`/"repeat until unambiguous" loop — but the official set still carries
  a divergent pair, so this is a hard gate failure, not merely a hidden-risk. The 2×2-Conv dedupe REPLICATES
  the parent exactly (10,000/10,000 incl. `g_adjacent_holes`/`g_black_rect`). **8,500 is the byte-equal floor;
  the ~2,000 B of dedupe is irreducible.**
- **Don't bother with MaxPool/UINT8 + Slice-shifts as a sub-floor.** Analyzed: replacing the 2×2-Conv dedupe
  with UINT8 Slice-shifts explodes tensor count (pad + 3 slices + 2 adds ≈ 9,341 > v2's 8,553); MaxPool can't
  shrink the Conv-adjacent F16 tensors without a Cast that eats the gain. The 2×2-Conv packs 3 shifts into one
  F16 tensor — already optimal. (And MaxPool is a novel op → grader-credit risk per traps.md.)
- **Don't compute the mask at 30×30** (each tensor 1,800 vs 800). Crop the black channel to 20×20, pad only
  the final single-channel BOOL mask back to 30×30. (Mask is identical at 30×30 vs 20×20-then-pad because
  input padding is all-zero → ch0=0 there → never an anchor.)
- **Don't use And/Or/Not/MaxPool** for the dedupe/dilation. Stays-in-vocab (Slice/Conv/Greater/Cast/Where/Mul/Pad)
  per traps.md "novel op chain" rule. The 2×2-Conv dedupe and output-Where introduce NO new op types.
- Sub-INT32 gather/sparse-init tricks are irrelevant here (no Gather); INT64 slice/pad indices are the only ints.
- **Don't skip the Clip (anchor_i8 binarization) step when using QLinearConv for dedupe.** If sum3_shifted_i8
  (range -8 to +1) is fed directly to the 2×2 dedupe conv, negative values near each other produce SPURIOUS
  POSITIVE outputs (e.g., -8 - (-8) - (-8) - (-8) = +16). The Clip {0,1} is mandatory. (Verified 2026-06-24.)
- **Don't try to replace Greater(dil_i8, 0) with Cast(dil_i8, BOOL).** MaxPool INT8 uses -128 (INT8_MIN) as the
  padding sentinel, NOT 0. Any negative nbr_check value near a border can appear in dil_i8 (since max(-128, -3) = -3 > INT8_MIN). Cast(-3, BOOL) = True → false positive fill. Greater(dil_i8, 0) → only dil_i8>0 (True). (Verified 2026-06-24.)
- **Don't re-attempt sub-3496 — Sho `scaled_cast` (3,496) is the proven correct floor.** The 2026-06-24
  "min correct = 4,672 / can't beat 4,066" proof was WRONG: it assumed a `Slice→ch0_i8→QLinearConv` path with
  separate anchor/nbr planes. Sho convs the scaled 4×4 kernel **directly on the F32 input** (no ch0 slice) and
  uses `Cast(int8)` as the threshold, deleting the 2000-B `ch0_f32`+`ch0_i8` pair AND the separate
  `sum3`/`anchor`/`nbr` planes. worker3 (2026-07-11) re-derived the floor at 3,496 by forced components (see
  Cost analysis + `hard_records/scaled_cast_floor_3496.md`). The head F32 seed (1296) is unavoidable on an F32
  input; the tail is minimal (P1/P2 probes both lose). WALL.
